Subject: Post-demo: latency head-to-head — proposed next tests

Hi Jillian / Aaron,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciated the level of detail on your production latency profile. A quick recap and a proposed next step for the competitive latency evaluation we discussed:

Summary from call:
- You see p95 ~ 180ms and p99 ~ 420ms on your current hyperscaler endpoint at steady-state during retail peak tests.
- Two model sizes in scope: retail-search-small (512 context) and ranking-large (4k context).
- Typical request mix: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% mid (65–512), 10% long (>512).

Proposed next steps (short, actionable):
1) Controlled head-to-head A/B: we run identical request stream to Redwood and to your hyperscaler endpoint for 3x 30-min windows (low/medium/high qps).
2) Measure p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and tokens/sec.
3) Collect representative request traces & sample payloads from your side (headers anonymized).
4) Redwood provides an initial test matrix and a cost/infra ask (nodes + expected tokens/sec).

Ask from your side:
- Permission to run the A/B tests against a short-lived test key for your hyperscaler endpoint (we will not store payloads beyond debug window).
- A sample trace or 1,000 request payloads that match the distribution above.

I attached a short worksheet (redwood-latency-20260517.xlsx) with the test matrix I had in mind. Can you confirm you’re comfortable with the plan and share the sample traces? If yes we'll finalize the schedule (we're aiming for next week).

Cc'ing Marissa and Ben internally — Marissa will own the bench run and Ben will surface cost implications for Dedicated vs hosted tests.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik / team — here's a recommended test matrix and infra ask based on Acme's traffic mix and Jillian's notes. I built this to minimize variance and produce comparable p95/p99 numbers.

High-level matrix (per model variant):
- Slot: 3 x 30 min windows (low/med/high) as proposed. Warm-up: 5 min, then measurement: 25 min. Repeat x3 to smooth noise.
- QPS targets: low=5 qps, med=20 qps, high=100 qps.
- Request distribution: short:64 (60%), mid:256–512 (30%), long:2k–4k (10%).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, mean latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, percentile kernel stalls, outlier traces (sample 1 per 1k).

Infra ask (recommended):
- For retail-search-small (512 context): 1x A10 or 1x V100 (8–16GB) per runner, 4 runners for high qps (auto-shard request streams).
- For ranking-large (4k context): 2x A100s (40GB) per runner recommended for p99 fidelity under long-contexts; start with 2 runners for high qps.
- Approx run time: two model variants x 3 windows x 30 min ~ 3 hours total wall time including warmups + buffer.

Expected throughput (rough estimates):
- retail-search-small: 10–18k tokens/sec per A10 runner at mixed mix; p95 in 40–90ms range expected depending on batch.
- ranking-large: 2–6k tokens/sec per A100 runner; p95 120–260ms depending on kv-cache warm state.

Success criteria proposal (for A/B):
- Redwood p95 <= Hyperscaler p95 - 10ms AND tokens/sec >= Hyperscaler tokens/sec * 0.85 for parity with cost bucket.
- Or Redwood p99 <= Hyperscaler p99 - 50ms.

Privacy / retention: we will mount an ephemeral storage volume and run a cron delete process to purge payloads and traces after 24h; logs will be scrubbed of headers per Acme guidance. We will capture only the minimal metadata necessary for debugging.

Attachments: request-hyperscaler-logs.txt (placeholder for Hyperscaler endpoints and sample trace names).

Risks / notes:
- Long-context runs (4k) are highly sensitive to batch sizing; we will run a short micro-benchmark on one runner to select kernel params before the main windows.
- If Hyperscaler provides a managed endpoint with unknown autoscaling, measurement noise may be higher — recommend running in their allocated staging cluster to stabilize.

If you all approve, I'll book nodes and draft the mutual action plan (one-pager) for Jillian/Aaron to sign off. Ben — can you add a simple cost row to the spreadsheet showing estimated $ for the test run in hosted vs reserved?

Marissa
